lines.meet: I'm Emre, and I open doors. When we reach a locked one, please let me do the talking, and please don't interrupt.
lines.meet_neighbour: Durnholde road, that's where I've seen you. I'm Emre, and I'm usually somewhere near a door.
lines.ask_home: Tell me where you're from, my friend. I like to know what kind of doors people grew up behind.
lines.ask_work: What did you do before? I've been guessing, and I'm usually wrong, which I enjoy.
lines.answer_home: Istanbul, the old bazaar quarter. I grew up above my uncle's lock shop, and I knew every door on our street.
lines.answer_work: Locksmith, from the age of nine. Thirty doors a week for most of my life, and I was never once a thief.
lines.chat_food: Turkish coffee, my friend, thick enough to stand a spoon in, with a little lokum on the side. Food is just what comes between coffees.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep well here, better than I did at home. There's nobody to open up the shop for in the morning.
lines.chat_missing: Turkish coffee in the morning, strong enough to stand a spoon in, and the cats waiting on my doorstep.
lines.chat_here: Every lock is a short conversation with somebody who isn't in the room. The people who made the locks here had very strange conversations.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're as quiet as a good lock. I've been trying to pick you for weeks.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, you interrupt a door the way you interrupt me. I'm learning patience from you, involuntarily.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you test a door before you touch it. My uncle would have taken you on as an apprentice.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you'd kick a door in that was never locked. I've watched you do it, and I've wept.
lines.tease_any: {name}, as we say in the bazaar, a good friend is a key you didn't know you had. Don't let it go to your head.
lines.tease_back: Very good, {name}. That one got through my defences.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's fair, {name}. There's a proverb for it somewhere, but it's fair.
lines.bristle: Some doors are better left shut, {name}. That's one of them.
lines.apologise: Forgive me, that was clumsy. I usually choose my words more carefully.
lines.double_down: I'll keep that one, my friend. It was true, and it was well put.
lines.needle_quiet: You stand there like a locked door, and I'm tired of picking it.
lines.needle_talker: You interrupt, my friend, every single time. It takes twice as long, and it was going to take long enough.
lines.needle_careful: You've been staring at it for ten minutes. Some locks you just open.
lines.needle_bold: You break doors that could be opened. It's like watching somebody tear a letter instead of unfolding it.
lines.needle_any: You called me a thief once, and I haven't forgotten. I was never a thief.
lines.bite_back: I've opened more doors than you've walked through, my friend. Don't tell me about patience.
lines.hurt: I see, then. I'll keep to myself for a while.
lines.laugh_off: My uncle said far worse with a deadbolt in his hand, my friend. Shall we go on?
lines.confide: {name}, I'm content here, and part of the reason is that the shop is gone, and everyone who wanted it kept a certain way. I lost an obligation, not a family, and I've been lighter since.
lines.listen: Thank you, {name}. I'll keep it locked away where nobody will find it.
lines.look_out: {name}, let me go first through that door. Whatever's behind it, I'd like to meet it before you do.
lines.accept: As you say, {name}. I'll go at your pace this once.
lines.deflect: I'm quite well, {name}, thank you. A scratch from an unfriendly hinge.
lines.check_in: {name}, you're hurt. Let me see it, slowly, I've got steady hands.
lines.blame: Somebody forced it, and it went badly, as forcing things does. I think you know who.
lines.thank: One door closes, another opens, and you held this one open for me. Thank you.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing, my friend. Rest, and let me make the coffee.
lines.worry: {name}, that was much too close. Sit, please, and let me see the damage.
lines.handed_down: I believe this was yours, my friend. I'll keep it oiled and in good order.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, please. I've got my picks, and that's all I've ever needed.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have been glad to hand it over, if anyone had asked me.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, I find I enjoy your company. That's a door I don't open for many people.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, I'd want you there when I try the door that beats me. That's the greatest honour I can think of.
lines.turn_grating: We don't fit, you and I, like a key in the wrong lock. Let's not force it.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll open your doors because it's my job. I won't hold them for you.
lines.make_up: {name}, we've been turning the wrong key. Let's try again, gently.
lines.defend: That's not fair, and I saw it all. Leave {name} be.
lines.friend_left: Doors are less interesting without {name} complaining about how long I take.
lines.friend_back: Ah, {name}, you've come back. Good, I've been saving a lock for you to watch.
lines.common_locks: I've opened locks since I was nine, in my uncle's shop above the bazaar. Every lock is a short conversation with somebody who isn't there, and you know that too.
lines.common_turkish: You speak Turkish, my friend! As we say at home, a familiar voice is the best key.
